transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-02
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE), Priya Nambiar (Redwood SE), Tom Garcia (AegisPay - Head of ML), Rina Patel (AegisPay - Platform Eng), Liam O'Connor (AegisPay - CTO)

Summary:
Quick sync on POC metrics from last week's load test, finalize canary/cutover plan, confirm monitoring and runbook ownership, decide on small A/B for latency vs cost config, next steps for rehearsal.

Topics:
- Canary traffic ramp plan
- Rollback thresholds and health checks
- Monitoring + alerting dashboards
- Runbook & on-call responsibilities
- Data residency / KMS access for Dedicated env
- Remaining blockers for go-live rehearsal

Action items (recap in meeting): see metadata list above.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'll kick off. we wanted to review the POC results and then move into the rollout plan - canary, cutover, runbooks. hi tom, rina, liam thanks for making time.
[00:18] Tom: hey alex, yeah good to be here. we ran the mixed traffic sim last saturday, overall throughput looked good, latency tail was a bit higher than we expected at peak though.
[00:27] Priya: (SE) quick note, some of the p95 spikes line up with the long context prompts you sent. we saw KV cache misses when sequences exceeded 2k tokens, that pushed GPU memory pressure on the dedicated nodes.
[00:45] Rina: yeah we saw that, and also a couple of 502s from our side when the ingress NLB timed out - looking at increasing idle timeout on the LB.
[01:02] Alex: good, so two things: we can tighten the batching window and enable prefix caching to mitigate the cache misses, and for the LB timeout that's a small infra change. priya, can you remind them what the suggested batching params are?
[01:18] Priya: sure, increase max_batch_wait_ms from 20 to 35 for the dedicated pool, and set max_tokens_per_request tuning to cap at 3k with graceful failure. also enable prefix_kv_cache with a 24h ttl for sessions. that should reduce repeated compute for similar prompts.
[01:37] Liam: curious on cost impact - increasing batching helps cost right? but does it affect latency SLOs for our interactive flows?
[01:46] Priya: yeah it's a tradeoff. batching reduces per-token cost but adds a slightly higher tail on individual requests. our recommendation for canary is to run a dual config A/B for 10% traffic: config A is lower latency (smaller batch window, higher cost), config B is cost-optimized (larger batching). measure user-facing p99 and CPU/GPU utilization for two weeks.
[02:05] Tom: that seems sensible. what's the proposed traffic ramp for canary? we want to avoid surprises during business hours.
[02:12] Alex: proposed plan: canary day 0: 1% traffic to Redwood config B for 4 hours (smoke), day 1: 5% for 12 hours, day 2: 10% for 24 hours with A/B split on that 10% (5% A, 5% B). rollback condition if p99 > 1200ms for read calls or error rate > 0.5% for 15 minutes. does that sound ok?
[02:38] Rina: yes but we need an on-call contact from redwood for the rehearsal window. last time we had a gap during the afternoon ramp.
[02:46] Alex: agreed, i'll be primary and priya will be secondary for the rehearsal. we will add escalation to eng-on-call at redwood if unresolved after 20 minutes.
[02:56] Priya: i'll also make sure instrumentation is in place - traces + logs populate the new Grafana dashboard and alerts fire into your pager duty integration. quick note: we recommend synthetic smoke tests that exercise long-context prompts and token-heavy flows.
[03:12] Liam: runbook question - who handles model fallback on error? do we automatically route to a smaller quantized variant or do we fail closed?
[03:21] Priya: two-tier fallback we suggest: 1) if inference errors increase, route to the quantized 8-bit variant on the same pool (lower quality but resilient); 2) if GPU memory pressure persists, route to hosted fallback in a different region (higher latency, preserves availability). both actions are automated with thresholds but require manual confirm for full traffic shift.
[03:43] Tom: i want to ensure data residency/KMS works in the dedicated env - we can't have keys leave our VPC. Rina, i'll need you to confirm the KMS admin rights.
[03:53] Rina: on that - we already submitted the KMS policy but need redwood to confirm the KMS integration flow. is that part of the runbook?
[03:59] Alex: yes, the runbook will include KMS handshake steps and verification. priya will include the exact commands and expected IAM roles.
[04:10] Priya: i'll add a verification checklist: kms key alias check, test encryption/decryption call, and sample audit log event for key usage.
[04:18] Liam: monitoring - what are the primary metrics we should watch during canary?
[04:23] Priya: p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, infer GPU utilization, queue length, batch size distribution, kv cache hit rate, and cost per 1k tokens. we will surface these in a per-route dashboard.
[04:36] Alex: also important: business metrics - cart conversion for the flows using the model, and model quality regressions - we should run a small eval set nightly during canary.
[04:46] Tom: can you include the eval harness in the runbook? we need nightly quality checks with thresholds that trigger manual rollback.
[04:52] Priya: yes, we'll add automated evals and threshold alerts. we'll also include a step to snapshot outputs for a 1% sample for manual review.
[05:03] Rina: about the A/B - how do we route percentage split? our infra uses feature flags via LaunchDarkly; can redwood accept header-based routing so LD can control the split?
[05:13] Alex: header-based routing works. we'll accept X-Redwood-Route header and apply the split in our smart router. Priya will provide the routing header examples.
[05:22] Priya: example: X-Redwood-Route: canaryA or canaryB. we also support traffic tags if you want to tie to LD.
[05:29] Liam: outage scenarios - what's the fastest rollback?
[05:33] Priya: fastest is to flip the LD flag to 0% for Redwood and fall back to your previous model. alternative is to set auto-rollback on our side so if error rate crosses threshold it will self-failover to the hosted fallback. both options are in the runbook.
[05:48] Tom: can we do a cutover rehearsal on the 8th as you suggested? prefer after hours, but include the Americas team on-call.
[05:56] Alex: yes, target rehearsal 2026-12-08 02:00-04:00 UTC. i'll send calendar invite after this call.
[06:03] Rina: one blocker - compliance asked for audit logs retention to be 13 months. is that configurable?
[06:10] Priya: default is 90 days in hosted, but for Dedicated we can enable extended retention and ship logs to your S3 with lifecycle. we'll include steps to enable that and the cost implications in the runbook.
[06:21] Liam: who signs off for go-live? we'll need CTO + Sec + Platform to approve after successful rehearsal.
[06:27] Alex: signoff checklist: successful 24h 10% canary with no severity incidents, eval thresholds met, runbook rehearsal successful, and SSO/KMS verified. signoff owners: Liam (CTO), Rina (Platform), Security lead (TBD).
[06:40] Tom: sounds good. one more - pricing for dedicated bursts during peak (we might need temporary burst capacity during Black Friday-like loads).
[06:48] Alex: we'll send an options sheet. short term we can enable burst nodes at X/hr and include a predicted cost for your observed QPS. i'll include in the follow-up.
[06:59] Priya: ok i'll prepare the dashboard links and the runbook draft and post to the shared drive.
[07:06] Rina: i'll confirm network rules and KMS policy by Friday.
[07:11] Alex: recap next steps - alex will share canary schedule + pricing, priya shares runbook + dashboards, rina and tom provide SLOs and prompts; schedule rehearsal for 12/08. any other items?
[07:23] Liam: none from me, thanks.
[07:25] Tom: thanks all.
[07:28] Alex: great thanks, meeting adjourned.
